claims.text: The as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution.
Surface segregation of Cu governs the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituent elements in the nanoparticles.
Surface-segregated Cu forms a Cu-enriched liquid layer during heating.
The Cu-enriched liquid-like surface layer nucleates and accelerates melting of the nanoparticle.
Localized Cu segregation initiates surface premelting.
The Cu-enriched liquid-like layer destabilizes the solid nanoparticle core and drives overall melting.
Reducing surface Cu suppresses formation of the Cu-enriched liquid-like layer.
Nanoparticles with reduced surface Cu will exhibit delayed melting onset.
Nanoparticles with reduced surface Cu will exhibit slower melting progression.
Baseline nanoparticles will develop a Cu-rich, liquid-like surface layer at temperatures significantly below the bulk melting point.
Formation of the Cu-rich surface layer in baseline nanoparticles will be followed by rapid melting of the entire nanoparticle.
Cu-depleted nanoparticles will have a higher temperature threshold for observable premelting than baseline nanoparticles.
As-synthesized uniformly composed nanoparticles are known to follow typical melting behavior observed in prior nanoparticle studies.
A comparison under inert-atmosphere in situ TEM heating from 600°C to 900°C at approximately 5°C/min can test the proposed mechanism.
Similar or lower premelting and overall melting onset in defect-free Cu-depleted nanoparticles relative to baseline nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
